transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Reed (Redwood SRE); Sara Lopez (Rivermark Head of ML), Tom Nguyen (Rivermark Infra), Raj Patel (CTO), Emily Chen (Product)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in focused on latency tuning — TTFT, streaming, seq len, kernel choices. Next steps and benchmarks assigned.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam: Alright folks, thanks for joining. we'll kick off, uh, 45 minutes on the clock. quick round robin—everyone still here?
[00:06] Sara: Yep, Sara here.
[00:07] Tom: Tom, yep.
[00:09] Priya: Priya here, ready.
[00:10] Liam: Great. Main agenda: review the numbers Priya sent yesterday, dig into TTFT improvements when we enable streaming and float16 kernels, and pick the next benchmark permutations.
[00:22] Priya: Cool. I'll start with the numbers. So we re-ran the hosted flow and dedicated sim on your staging config. Baseline for seq_len 128 with streaming off, float32 default kernels, we saw median token latency around 18ms per token, TTFT about 140ms, p95 end-to-end generation for a 64-token response was ~340ms.
[00:38] Priya: With streaming on and enabling float16 execution (we used the quantized path + continuous batching hints), TTFT dropped to ~95ms and p95 to 220ms for the same prompt set. Note: streaming helps TTFT because we start sending partial tokens, so perceived latency is lower.
[01:00] Tom: Quick question — when you say float16, is that the fp16 path within our current runtime or a new kernel build? We have cert issues with the experimental kernels on our staging nodes.
[01:08] Priya: Right, good call. The float16 path used the standard runtime float16 code path, not the experimental kernel. But we also tested a 'cutlass-optimized' kernel variant — that's what we flagged as experimental — which shaved another ~12% off token latency in synthetic runs, but it increased memory by ~8%.
[01:31] Marcus: That memory increase is what worries me. We saw an OOM event last week on the smaller node. What was the headroom during the cutlass runs?
[01:38] Priya: On the node we used, headroom dropped from about 22% to 14%. So still under but closer to threshold. That's why we recommended enabling burst capacity or reserving a slightly larger instance for dedicated.
[01:50] Sara: Our p95 target for production is 250ms or lower for 64-token responses. So the cutlass path looks promising as long as it's reliable.
[01:58] Priya: Agreed. Also sequence length matters — when we bumped to seq_len 256, p95 increased to ~410ms with default kernels, streaming on helped but we still were at ~300ms p95. At seq_len 512, default was ~730ms p95; float16+cutlass brought that down to ~540ms p95.
[02:20] Emily: Can you remind me what chunking or prompt truncation you recommended? Our product team is worried about user-visible truncation.
[02:27] Priya: For short responses, keep seq_len to 128-256. For longer completions, we suggested prefix caching — the KV cache preserves the prompt context so only new tokens are computed. That reduces effective compute for many flows.
[02:39] Tom: Our staging infra currently doesn't persist KV cache between requests; we flush after each session for security. Is that a blocker?
[02:45] Priya: If you can't persist across sessions, we can still do prefix caching per session. The biggest win is when you can reuse cached prefixes across repeat queries (like templated prompts). If compliance requires flush, we can instead use batching and lower token budgets.
[02:58] Raj: Any security concerns with KV cache and PII? We need to confirm redaction.
[03:03] Liam: Standard approach — we recommend token-level redaction hooks and KMS-managed keys; Redwood's privacy modes can be toggled. But we'll share the security note. I'll put it in the repo.
[03:13] Sara: Cool. Back to kernels — what's the fallback story if cutlass fails at runtime? We need graceful degradation.
[03:20] Priya: Absolutely. The runtime supports kernel fallbacks automatically. If the optimized kernel raises memory pressure or errors, we fallback to default kernel variant. We also support canarying kernel versions per rollout.
[03:31] Tom: Great. For our POC we want to validate two axes: seq_len 512 vs 256 and kernel variant default vs cutlass, streaming on/off. Can we get a matrix and expected p95 numbers?
[03:41] Priya: Yes — that's what I ran. I'll attach the spreadsheet link in the follow-up. Quick numbers: 256/default/streaming on => ~300ms p95; 256/float16/cutlass/streaming => ~240ms p95; 512/default/streaming on => ~540ms p95; 512/float16/cutlass/streaming => ~420-540ms range depending on batch size and memory headroom.
[04:05] Marcus: Batch size impact? We saw higher throughput but tail got worse at larger batch sizes.
[04:10] Priya: Right, continuous batching increases throughput but can add queueing latency for the first token. For TTFT we keep batch_size low for priority traffic; for background jobs we can increase it. We recommended hybrid: priority route with immediate dispatch (small batch), background with batched lane.
[04:26] Sara: On pricing, Liam, you mentioned float16 kernels might change unit costs?
[04:31] Liam: Correct — float16 reduces compute cost per token but if cutlass increases memory and forces a larger instance, unit cost could go up. We'll run a cost-sensitivity calc and share a delta table.
[04:43] Raj: Can you also include projected cost for 99th percentile spikes when we have concurrent sessions hitting model?
[04:50] Liam: Yep, we'll model concurrency scenarios and show conservative reserve capacity.
[04:55] Emily: Any weird transcription errors in the tests? I mean, were there mis-identified tokens or hallucinations because of quantization?
[05:01] Priya: We ran the regression evals on the eval set and saw negligible quality delta for float16, at most 0.6% degradation on long-form coherence metrics. For short responses it's within noise. We'll push the diff in the quality notebook.
[05:17] Tom: About streaming — does Redwood stream partial tokens (token-by-token) or chunked deltas? We're seeing partial chunks cause issues in our websocket layer.
[05:25] Priya: We stream deltas (we flush tok groups every 50-100ms depending on throughput). You can adjust chunk sizes. If you need per-token streaming we can enable a lower-latency pipeline but it sometimes increases CPU overhead.
[05:38] Tom: Ok good to know. That helps our websocket buffer sizing.
[05:41] Marcus: One ops note — the staging node that OOM'd had an older driver. We suspect the optimized kernel is more sensitive to driver version. Recommend aligning driver to our validated list.
[05:52] Priya: Yep, validated driver + CUDA runtime recommended. I'll include the exact versions in the doc.
[05:58] Sara: For the next run, can we also test a scenario with prefix caching allowed but with PII redaction hook enabled so we mimic prod privacy constraints?
[06:06] Priya: Yes, that's on the matrix. We'll simulate redaction overhead (adds a small CPU pass per prompt) — it increased TTFT by roughly 10-15ms in our runs.
[06:17] Liam: Quick check — agreed matrix: seq_len {256,512}, kernel {default,cutlass}, precision {fp32,fp16}, streaming {on,off}, prefix caching {on with redaction, off}. That should cover most.
[06:34] Emily: Estimated time to run all permutations?
[06:36] Priya: If we parallelize across two staging nodes, about 24-36 hours for stable runs at good sample sizes. If you only have one node it will take longer.
[06:44] Tom: We have two nodes free this week. I'll reserve them Monday.
[06:49] Priya: Great. I'll prepare the run script and configs.
[06:52] Liam: Any blockers from legal or security to run these?
[06:55] Sara: Security flagged nothing new as long as we use KMS for logs and scrub PII — which we will.
[07:02] Priya: Ok next — quality regression alarms. We set a guardrail to alert if eval delta >1% on our coherence metric; Ri—, Sara, do you want that threshold adjusted?
[07:11] Sara: Keep it tight for now, 1% is fine. We can relax after we see the delta.
[07:15] Liam: Good. I'll include alerting config in the doc.
[07:18] Tom: One more infra question — are there kernel-specific CPU pins we should be aware of? The cutlass path moved some work to the host.
[07:26] Priya: It does increase host CPU usage modestly — about +5-8% observed. We'll call that out in the note so you can size the host accordingly.
[07:35] Marcus: Thanks.
[07:37] Priya: Alright I'll share the spreadsheet now — link: (inserted in chat) https://redwood.link/perf/rm-poc-2027-05-18 (note: shared doc, see sheet "summary").
[07:50] Liam: Perfect. Let's quickly capture action items. Priya — rerun matrix with seq512 and cutlass vs default, streaming on; attach raw logs.
[07:59] Priya: Yep, will do.
[08:01] Liam: Liam — I'll send pricing delta and security note by tomorrow.
[08:05] Liam: Tom — confirm staging node availability and memory headroom.
[08:08] Tom: I'll open a ticket and confirm.
[08:10] Sara: I'll validate prompt set and p95 target.
[08:13] Liam: Cool. Any other questions?
[08:16] Raj: Not from me. Thanks.
[08:17] Emily: No, thanks.
[08:18] Liam: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the doc and pick a time next week to review results.
[08:23] (call ends)
